agent_vs_you: The agent's tree was right: a qwen-lettered black end card, then assemble with the user's clip first. Its extra said exactly what was wanted: 'retain all 7 seconds unchanged with original audio; hold end-card.png for 2 seconds'. assemble.js ignores per-piece timing. With seconds 9 and two pieces it sets share = 4.5, gives the clip min(7, 4.5) = 4.5 s and the picture 4.5 s, and so silently cut a third of the user's footage, which the catalogue says assemble keeps 'as they are'. This is the same defect as D23a. I would get 7 + 2 from today's tools by making the card a 2-second clip first (assemble on the card alone, seconds 2), then joining the two clips with seconds 0, which keeps each clip at its own length. The agent had no way to know the even split existed, because the catalogue only promises 'the exact length'.

your_plan.say: I'll make the black end card with your two centred white lines, then add it for exactly 2 silent seconds after your full 7-second clip, keeping the clip's own sound.

params.prompt_or_change: Solid pure black background with two centred lines of clean white sans-serif lettering, large and comfortably inside the frame: "Ready for takeoff?" and directly below it "@flightschool". Nothing else: no logo, no border, no other text.

steps.why: A designed card with exact, read-back lettering on qwen. It matches the clip's 16:9 (1280x720). This was already correct in the agent's run.

params.prompt_or_change: Hold the end card for exactly 2 seconds, silent.

steps.why: With one picture, assemble gives it the whole 2.0 s, plus a silent audio track.

params.prompt_or_change: The full clip with its sound, then the end card.

steps.why: seconds 0 keeps each clip at its own length: 7.0 s of untouched footage and audio, then 2.0 s of silent card, 9.0 s total. No music input.

fix: Same as D23a: assemble.js must honour per-piece durations (extra 'durations: 7, 2', or 'hold X for N seconds'). It must never shorten a supplied clip to make an even share unless the user asked to cut it. When a total is set, clips keep their full length and pictures get what remains (here 9 - 7 = 2 s). If the total cannot be met without cutting the user's clip, the node should fail or flag rather than cut.
evidence: radio-lines.mp4 is 1280x720, 7.0 s, with audio. The output radio-lines-with-end-card.mp4 is 9.02 s, with scene changes at 3.36 s (cockpit 2) and 4.52 s (end card). silencedetect finds silence from 4.51 s to the end. A 1 fps strip shows cockpit footage for 0–4 s and the end card from 5 s on, reading 'Ready for takeoff?' / '@flightschool' in white on black, centred and correct. end-card.png is 640x352. So the clip lost its last 2.5 s and the card ran 4.5 s, exactly the share = 9/2 split in assemble.js. The grader is right.
